reasons.text: The preference tier Series A Preferred is fully paid ($2,000,000.00). Above this exit value, the next dollar goes to the next tier's preference (Seed Preferred, Investor P's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount), Investor Q's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount), Investor R's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount), Investor S's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount), Investor T's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount) and Investor U's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount)).

The preference tier Seed Preferred, Investor P's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount), Investor Q's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount), Investor R's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount), Investor S's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount), Investor T's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount) and Investor U's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount) is fully paid ($4,000,000.00). Above this exit value, the next dollar goes to the residual, shared as common.

Common reaches $0.25 per share, the strike on the 500,000 options at that price. Above this exit value they are in the money and exercised: their holders pay the strike, which is added to the proceeds, and share in the residual as common.

Seed Preferred converts to common. At this exit value its as-converted share (2,000,000 common shares at $0.5000 each = $1,000,000.00) equals its 1x preference of $1,000,000.00. Below it, staying preferred pays more; above it, converting pays more.

Investor P's SAFE switches from its Cash-Out Amount to its Conversion Amount. Its 638,888.89 conversion shares ($500,000.00 ÷ the Liquidity Price of $0.782609) are worth $0.782609 each here, $500,000.00 in all, which equals its purchase amount. Below this exit value the Cash-Out Amount pays more; above it, the Conversion Amount does. It converts together with Investor Q's SAFE and Investor R's SAFE. On its own, converting would pay it only $475,000.00 here, less than its cash; with all of them converting, each gets its fixed share of the Liquidity Capitalization, which pays more above this exit value, so they convert.
